payload.body_html: Hi everyone!

Hi everyone,

We're building Solstack (solstack.xyz), a set of browser-based tools for Solana. It's for developers who create and manage tokens, and for traders who want to check a token before they buy it.

For token creators: mint SPL and Token-2022 tokens, launch on pump.fun, letsbonk and Meteora, send tokens to a list of wallets with a single signature, airdrop to every holder of a token, and lock or vest supply.

For traders: a 0–100 safety score for any token, a check on whether its liquidity is actually locked, and a way to get back the SOL tied up in empty token accounts.

In this series we'll share what we learned building it, including the parts of Solana that surprised us.

Hi All!

Hello from Houston. 👋

Naveen. Software architect, about seventeen years in, most of it building .NET and Python systems for government agencies. That work means a lot of forms, workflows and business rules that arrive from statute rather than from anyone's product roadmap, which has shaped how I think about software more than I expected it to.

Lately it has been Azure, RAG and ML.NET. The recurring lesson is that the model is never the hard part. Deciding what the system should refuse to do is the hard part.

Read here for a long time, finally made an account. Working on a first post about form builders and validation rules that are themselves invalid, which turns out to be more interesting than it sounds.

Hey everyone 👋

I'm building proxy infrastructure for developers — the plumbing between a scraper or an AI agent and the site it's trying to reach. We launch in October, so right now most of my time goes to reading error messages and working out which ones are actually the proxy's fault. (Fewer than you'd think.)

I'll be writing here about the unglamorous side of web data: proxy errors, why requests pass locally and fail in CI, and what bot detection actually looks at.

If you're stuck on a proxy or blocking issue, feel free to ping me — happy to help debug.
